prs.title: fix: send notifications/cancelled on request timeout and caller cancellation
prs.author: dragogargo
prs.reason: [llm] cluster primary: RequestResponder.cancel() incorrectly sends a JSON-RPC error response for cancelled requests, violating the MCP spec (tracked as issue #2480). The spec requires receivers to send no response and instead emit a notifications/cancelled message. (2 PRs)
prs.short_reason: [llm] cluster primary: RequestResponder.cancel() incorrectly sends a JSON-RPC error response for cancelled requests, violating the MCP spec (tracked as issue #2480). The spec requires receivers to send no response and instead emit a notifications/cancelled message. (2 PRs)
prs.cluster_pick_reason: PR #2514 is the complete fix: it removes the incorrect error-response send (same as #2493) and additionally emits the spec-mandated CancelledNotification, handling both the timeout and caller-cancellation cases per its title. PR #2493 removes the wrong behavior but leaves nothing in its place, so the spec-required notification is never sent.

prs.title: fix(shared): make UrlElicitationRequiredError pickle-safe (refs #2431)

(2 PRs)
prs.short_reason: [llm] cluster primary: UrlElicitationRequiredError (and MCPError subclasses) are not pickle-safe: Exception.__reduce_ex__ reconstructs via cls(*self.args) using (code, message, data), which mismatches the subclass constructor signature (elicitations, message=None), raising TypeError on unpickle (issue #2431). prs.cluster_pick_reason: PR #2555 is the more complete fix: it adds __reduce__ directly on UrlElicitationRequiredError with a clean round-trip through (self._elicitations, self.message), includes test coverage in tests/shared/test_exceptions.py, and explicitly closes #2431. PR #2478 introduces a _restore_mcp_error dispatcher but its diff shows no caller for the helper, making it appear incomplete — the broader MCPError.__reduce__ wiring that would invoke it is absent from the shown diff.
